key_insight: In MAPbI3 perovskite crystals, optically oriented photogenerated holes can resonantly cool nuclear spins, with the effect identified through modulation-frequency-dependent Hanle resonances.
engineering_relevance: This reveals a spin-interaction pathway in perovskites that could matter for designing optoelectronic and spintronic devices where carrier localization and nuclear-spin dynamics influence performance.
method: Hanle-effect measurements versus magnetic field and modulation frequency
In-plane rotation test to check nuclear-species symmetry
evidence_signal: The resonance in the Hanle curve shifts to higher magnetic fields as modulation frequency increases, and its rotation invariance plus line shape indicate involvement of 207Pb nuclei and holes with negative g-factor.
watch_item: The conclusion depends on identifying strongly localized holes as the main contributors, so device conditions that alter localization may change or suppress the effect.
paper_title: Resonant cooling of nuclear spins by optically-oriented holes in MAPbI$_3$ perovskite crystals
